title: Geometric and coefficient-domain realization of base change
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\prime\to Y$, $g\prime:X\prime\to X$ and $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ form a Cartesian square, so $f g\prime=g f\prime$ and $X\prime\simeq X\times_Y Y\prime$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use the adjunction-mate ordinary exchange and the compactification-defined compact-support exchange [def-exchange-projection], with completed integral pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Every corner is Noetherian, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite dimension. There is a nonnegative uniform bound on the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, including empty fibres; if $f$ is proper, so is $f'$. Compactifications exist, and their open factors are quasi-compact.
The actual exchanges
$$g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K,\qquad g^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!g'^*K$$
have the following isomorphism domains. For the first map require $f$ proper or $g$ smooth. At finite etale coefficients use bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology; its pro-etale transport requires an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], bounded constructible in the smooth case. At integral coefficients use the completed exchange and compatible finite-reduction etale-origin witnesses. At $E$ use a specified admissible integral lattice and the raw rationalized exchange; at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use admissible common-stage representatives stable under finite overfields. For smooth exchange the lattice and comparison hypotheses are exactly those of [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] and [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch]; a conclusion in $D^b_c$ additionally requires the uniform finite-level constructibility and interval bounds stated there. Without those landing bounds only the ambient completed isomorphism is asserted.
For the second map no smoothness of $g$ is needed. Use bounded finite torsion etale inputs, their witnessed finite pro-etale transports, and at integral and field stages the derived-complete constructible inputs with compatible etale-origin reductions and the specified lattice/common-stage presentations and uniform landing bounds of [thm-cbc-complete-proetale], [thm-cbc-finite-extension], [thm-cbc-qbar]. The maps coincide with those supplied by the respective finite, completed and transported base-change theorems, and respect identity, pasting, refinement and composition on those domains. No exchange for discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small etale site is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [fix-lem-exchanges] once and retain its finite-datum identification, finite laws, completed ordinary and support laws, support naturality, integral model and mate identifications, square naturality and normalization. Retain its rational/common-stage support laws and common-stage smooth assertion for the square clauses.

proof.text: For proper rational exchange apply the completed proper clause to the supplied lattice integral object and its compatible origins. It supplies constructible endpoints and an invertible arrow in their full subcategory. Localize that arrow and transport along the lattice rationalization isomorphism. Use the identity integral endpoint identifications and the localized arrow for the constructible representation; its representation equation is naturality, after computing localization on a pure tensor. For proper common stages apply [thm-weil-pbc-qbar] and retain invertibility and the finite-overfield formula.

proof.text: For smooth rational exchange apply [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] to the transposed square and specified admissible lattice. Apply it also at every finite coefficient field, taking the constructible conclusion only from square admissibility. The common-stage smooth clause is the corresponding specialization of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Proof irrelevance identifies the geometric Fact witnesses without altering any lattice domain.

proof.text: For compact support, finite etale exchange is invertible by the existing finite-coefficient instance, and [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] applies to each retained origin. Apply [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] to the specified complete object and compatible origins. Retain the rational and common-stage support laws from [fix-lem-exchanges]. Apply [thm-cbc-qbar] for existence, finite-stage and descended invertibility; use [fix-lem-exchanges] again for the common-stage representative and independence predicate on the same square. No smoothness is introduced.
